summary: In Proxy Mobile IPv6, traffic from a mobile node is usually tunneled to a Local Mobility Anchor. Localized routing instead routes packets directly between the access gateways of the two communicating nodes. This document defines Diameter support for that.

eli5.summary: Rather than sending a letter through headquarters, two neighbors pass it over the fence. This explains how the control system permits that shortcut.

questions: how does diameter authorize localized routing
what is the mip6 feature vector avp
subtitle: How a AAA server can authorize direct routing between two Proxy Mobile IPv6 gateways using Diameter.

tldr.problem: Proxy Mobile IPv6 localized routing lets two gateways exchange packets directly instead of going through a Local Mobility Anchor, but an operator may want each such session to be authorized first.
tldr.mechanism: The gateway (MAG) or anchor (LMA) acts as a Diameter client and asks the AAA server in an AA-Request carrying the two mobile node identifiers and a capability flag. The server answers with the flag set or cleared.
tldr.outcome: It defines one new capability flag, INTER_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED, and shows three example signaling flows that fit the localized routing protocol of RFC 6705.

today: RFC 7156 is a Proposed Standard published in April 2014, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It works together with the localized routing protocol in RFC 6705 and the Diameter applications RFC 5779 and RFC 7155.

sections.title: Why Localized Routing Needs Authorization
sections.content:
In Proxy Mobile IPv6 (PMIPv6, RFC 5213), packets from a Mobile Node (MN) are normally tunneled by its Mobile Access Gateway (MAG) to a Local Mobility Anchor (LMA). RFC 5213 allows one shortcut, called local routing, when the MN and its Correspondent Node (CN) are attached to the same MAG.

That shortcut does not cover the typical cases where the MN and CN sit behind different MAGs and are registered to the same LMA or to different LMAs. RFC 6279 describes that problem, and RFC 6705 defines the localized routing protocol that sets up a path between two MAGs.

This document adds the missing control piece: authorization. It uses Diameter (RFC 6733) for the exchange between the PMIPv6 entities (MAG or LMA) and a AAA server in the same PMIPv6 domain. It covers scenarios A11, A12 and A21 from RFC 6279.
sections.eli5: Passing notes directly is faster than sending them through headquarters. This document explains how to ask permission before starting.

sections.title: The Reference Architecture
sections.content:
The reference architecture has a AAA server holding policy and profile data, plus several LMAs and MAGs. The MAG and the LMA both MUST be able to act as Diameter clients, and they talk to the AAA server using Diameter and to each other using PMIPv6.

The document ties the three RFC 6279 scenarios to the placement of the nodes:

  • A12: the MN and CN share the same MAG but belong to different LMAs in the same provider domain.
  • A21: the MN and CN are attached to different MAGs but belong to the same LMA.
  • A11: the MN and CN share the same MAG and the same LMA.

In every case, the interaction with the AAA server is what authorizes the localized routing service.
sections.eli5: There is one front desk (the AAA server), some regional offices (the LMAs) and some local post boxes (the MAGs). The post boxes and offices all know how to ask the front desk for permission.

sections.title: The AVPs and the New Flag
sections.content:
Diameter carries data in Attribute Value Pairs (AVPs). This document reuses several and adds one new flag value. The AA-Request is the one defined by the Diameter NASREQ application (RFC 7155).

  • User-Name (AVP Code 1) carries the MN-Identifier of the mobile node.
  • PMIP6-IPv4-Home-Address (AVP Code 505) carries the MN's IPv4 home address.
  • MIP6-Home-Link-Prefix (AVP Code 125) carries the MN's home network prefix.
  • MIP6-Feature-Vector is a 64-bit flags field that tells the AAA server which capabilities are supported.

The new flag is INTER_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED with the value 0x0002000000000000. When a MAG or LMA sets it in a request, it says that direct routing between MNs anchored to different MAGs may be provided. When the home AAA server sets it in the answer, that routing is authorized. A cleared flag, in a request or an answer, means the procedure is not supported or not authorized.

MAGs and LMAs that comply with this document MUST support this policy feature on a per-MN and per-subscription basis.
sections.eli5: The request is a form with the names of the two people and a checkbox that says "may these two pass notes directly?". The front desk ticks the box to say yes or leaves it empty to say no.

sections.title: Example Signaling Flows
sections.content:
Authorization can happen during network access authentication, before localized routing starts. The pre-authorized pairs of LMA and prefix sets can then be downloaded, and localized routing can begin once a packet's destination matches one of the received prefixes.

The document also shows three flows in which a Diameter client asks at the moment a packet is seen:

  • MAG-initiated, scenario A12 (Figure 2): MAG1 sees a packet from MN1 to MN2, compares the LMA addresses in the binding cache entries and finds different LMAs. It sends an AA-Request with the feature vector and two User-Name AVPs. If the AA-Answer is positive, MAG1 sends a Localized Routing Initialization (LRI) message to each LMA and gets a Localized Routing Acknowledge (LRA) back, as in RFC 6705.
  • LMA-initiated, scenario A21 (Figure 3): LMA1 sees the packet, finds that both MNs belong to it, and asks the AAA server with INTER_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED set. On success it continues with the LRI and LRA exchange toward the two MAGs.
  • LMA-initiated, scenario A11 (Figure 4): the same flow with both MNs on one MAG, using the LOCAL_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED bit from RFC 5779.

If LRA_WAIT_TIME expires, the client SHOULD ask for authorization again before the LRI is retransmitted, up to a maximum of LRI_RETRIES.
sections.eli5: Whoever notices two neighbors talking asks the front desk first. If the answer is yes, they tell both sides to start passing notes directly. If nobody answers in time, they ask again before trying again.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Notes
sections.content:
The security considerations of the NASREQ application (RFC 7155) and the Diameter Proxy Mobile IPv6 application (RFC 5779) also apply. The authorization depends on the existing trust relationship between the MAG or LMA and the AAA server.

The RFC adds a privacy warning. An authorized MAG could, in principle, track which MAG each participating mobile node is anchored to. If such a MAG were compromised or controlled by a bad actor, that would be a privacy breach. The traffic from a compromised MAG might stand out, so monitoring for excessive queries from MAGs might be worthwhile.
sections.eli5: The front desk trusts the post boxes that ask it questions. A bad post box could watch where everyone lives, so it helps to notice one that asks far too many questions.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The only IANA action is a new value in the "Mobility Capability Registry" that RFC 5447 created for use with the MIP6-Feature-Vector AVP. The new value is INTER_MAG_ROUTING_SUPPORTED.
sections.eli5: A new checkbox is added to the official list of checkboxes, so everybody uses the same one.
